critique: The note delivers the equality-inclusive weak-order maximum, finite-sample validity, exact fixed-k algorithms, effect inversion, and an explicit NP-completeness reduction with its load-bearing midrank lemma proved in the manuscript. The computational frontier is limited to XP versus variable-k NP-completeness for explicitly listed rationally weighted supports; FPT versus W[1]-hardness and uniform balance-generated supports remain open, so the result is not a complete parameterized or restricted-design frontier. The completely randomized-design theorem supplies fixed-k polynomial evaluation but neither a general-k classification nor the stronger closed-form simplification available under altered tie-breaking. The projected paper score is constrained by this narrow computational scope and by the absence of power, informativeness, or applied evidence showing when the worst-case envelope is useful rather than vacuous, although the proved results clear the field-contribution floor. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
